description: The graph illustrates the training loss over time for two methods—Vanilla and SepLLM—during the training of a large language model. The x-axis represents the training time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250,000, with major gridlines at intervals of 50,000. The y-axis shows the loss value, scaled linearly from 2.40 to 2.75. Both methods begin with a high loss value near 2.75 and exhibit a decreasing trend as training progresses. The Vanilla method is represented by a purple line with circular markers, while the SepLLM method is shown as a red line with circular markers. The SepLLM line consistently remains below the Vanilla line, indicating a faster or more efficient reduction in loss. At the end of the training period (around 250,000 seconds), the SepLLM loss stabilizes near 2.50, while the Vanilla loss is slightly higher, around 2.52. A green dashed horizontal line at a loss of 2.50 is shown, and a green box highlights the region from approximately 200,000 to 250,000 seconds, where the SepLLM loss is noted to be 1.26 times lower than the Vanilla loss at that point, suggesting a significant performance improvement.
